failure_modes: If a temporal blend (C009-C011) is applied, the observed-node contrast sign changes could shift regional attention in the wrong direction at nodes where the last-window rate opposes the first-window rate, displacing surrounding coordinates without affinity benefit.

If pointcloud_delta_A is narrowed (C001) without spatial-scale evidence, the robust kernel could over-weight near-coincident endpoint pairs and increase unnecessary displacement of surrounding coordinates.
If teacher_neighbors is broadened (C007) without intact-teacher dispersion evidence, mode coverage may include competing directions and dilute the endpoint reward signal.
Retaining the incumbent risks missing a genuine time-conditioned contrast advantage if H001's falsifier is later rejected by joint diagnostics.
rationale: Analyst's temporal evidence (F003-F005) shows landmark contrast curves with multiple sign changes and strong sign conflicts, and polynomial fits rejected with extrapolation disallowed, so a time-conditioned contrast rule (H001) is plausible but not established as better than the incumbent static rule; the falsifier (constant rule with equal fit fidelity and no sign-change mismatch) is not excluded by the delivered rows. The registered temporal choices (C008-C011) change only a blend scalar/attention at observed score nodes and cannot be shown to improve the primary endpoint affinity objective from these observational curves alone. The spatial choices (C001-C003 pointcloud_delta_A, C005-C007 teacher_neighbors) are not supported by any delivered spatial-scale or dispersion evidence in this turn, and C004 region_index is a static regional selection with no supporting regional_effects rows read. Per D4.1, evidence does not provide a defensible expected advantage for any offered edit, so the incumbent is retained. Temperatures remain fixed and untouched.
